implementation.name: Wonder Swan (MiSTer)
implementation.notes: Source availability (T5.4): open -- the repository carries 51 HDL source files (4 systemverilog, 2 verilog, 45 vhdl) alongside 9 prebuilt .rbf binaries. There is no open_source column in the delivered schema (data-model.md §1.9 deleted the proposed core table together with its flags); the presence of hdl_language_id and of implementation_path rows is how that fact is stated here. Machine mapping: hand-mapped, not MRA-setname-derived -- a console core ships no MRA files. The core reimplements the Bandai WonderSwan and WonderSwan Color; the distribution's _Console/WonderSwan Color.mgl names <rbf>_Console/WonderSwan</rbf>, giving machine_id wswan and MAME wscolor -> machine_id wswan. Every id was checked against extract/machine.json; MAME's own cloneof relation supplied the parent where the obvious shortname is a clone. License: https://github.com/MiSTer-devel/WonderSwan_MiSTer/blob/main/LICENSE is the verbatim GNU GPL version 2 text, and the grant in https://github.com/MiSTer-devel/WonderSwan_MiSTer/blob/main/WonderSwan.sv reads "either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version" -- hence GPL-2.0-or-later. hdl_language_id: no single HDL family reaches 90% of the 51 source files (4 systemverilog, 2 verilog, 45 vhdl), excluding the shared framework directory. accuracy_id omitted: the repository makes no timing-fidelity claim this build could verify.
